It was a win-or-go-home game for the Comets, and they live to fight another day after dominating the Aviators in Game 2 of the Championship Series in a 7-2 victory.
Player of the Day
While Zach Ehrhard and James Tibbs III led the way with the bat, it was Landon Knack’s outstanding work as a starter that allowed the Comets to open a five-run lead before the Aviators could think about entering the game. Doing a complete 180 from the previous game’s pitching struggles, Landon Knack didn’t walk anyone and struck out eight in 6.1 one-run innings.
For anyone closely monitoring Knack’s September stats, this was hardly a surprising development, considering he had come into the game with 11.2 scoreless innings this month, 7.2 of them in Triple-A with the Comets.
Triple-A Oklahoma City
The middle-infield combo of Noah Miller and Hyeseong Kim reached in front of Zach Ehrhard in the third inning, and the Comets’ leadoff hitter drove them both in to give his team a lead they would maintain until the end.
Between the third and fifth innings, the Comets scored six of their eventual seven runs, all unanswered, capped by a James Tibbs III three-run bomb, doing what he has done basically the whole year.
The Comets showed discipline to put the ball in play, ending the game with only five strikeouts, under half the total of the Aviators’ lineup. Ryan Fitzgerald, the veteran who was the only Comet to strike out multiple times, got on the scoreboard with a solo shot in the eighth.
Not only dominant, but Knack also found a way to be extremely efficient and could’ve easily gone further than the 6.1 innings he covered, getting the hook when he was at just 81 pitches. Recently demoted flamethrower Seth Halvorsen contributed a scoreless frame with a walk and two strikeouts. The Aviators’ second and final run came against Paul Gervase in the ninth inning.
Transactions
The Comets placed outfielder Chris Newell and pitcher Jackson Ferris on the Development List. The Dodgers optioned pitcher Kyle Hurt and outfielder Josue De Paula to the Comets. Lastly, they activated Emmet Sheehan as well.

The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants.
They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League West title and 13 out of 14 on Thursday.
Entering the final week of the season, the Dodgers can clinch a bye week with a magic number of three over the Braves.
Batter of the week
Kyle Tucker is starting to turn things around at the plate, and followed up an excellent series the previous weekend in Miami with nine hits in 20 at-bats, with three home runs and two doubles, with six walks and just one strikeout.
Honorable mention goes to Mookie Betts, who tied a Dodgers record with three doubles on Saturday, part of a stretch of three consecutive games with at least three hits. Will Smith found his power again with two home runs and a double, and Alex Freeland reached base eight times in 14 trips to the plate, including a home run and a double.
Pitcher of the week
Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched seven scoreless innings with seven strikeouts to beat the Reds on Tuesday, his third straight seven-inning start in September. Yamamoto this season has allowed zero or one run in 14 of his 27 starts.
Honorable mention goes to Justin Wrobleski, who retired all nine batters he faced with three strikeouts while starting Thursday’s division clincher in Cincinnati, and to Landon Knack, who got the win in that game with four scoreless innings in relief. Also to Emmet Sheehan, who continued his strong six-week run with nine strikouts in 5 1/3 scoreless frames on Sunday.

Miscellany
Half a hundred: The Dodgers have won 10 games in a row at home, and Sunday’s win was their 50th win at Dodger Stadium this season. That’s six straight years with 50 wins at home, plus seven straight full seasons dating back to 2019. Since moving into Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers won 50 home games 12 times in 51 full seasons through 2014. But since 2015, they’ve won at least 50 games at home 10 times in 11 full seasons.
A crowded 10-K: Tyler Glasnow beat the Giants on Friday with a strong six innings, including 10 strikeouts. Glasnow is the eighth different Dodgers pitcher with a 10-strikeout game this season, the most in franchise history. No other MLB team this year has more than five such pitchers.
Parliamentary procedure: After making the All-Star team as a starter with the Kansas City Royals in 2025, left-hander Kris Bubic was on the 60-day injured list when the Dodgers acquired him just ahead of the August 3 trade deadline. Now he’s pitching in relief, angling for a spot on the postseason roster. With his appearance on Wednesday, Bubic became the 33rd different Dodgers pitcher used this season. So far, Bubic has four strikeouts in 2 2/3 innings in three appearances. “It’s just funk,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday of Bubic. “It’s nothing overpowering, but there’s just funky swings, soft contact. I see him as a neutral pitcher, gets left and right out. I like those converted starters, because he knows how to navigate lineups.”
A quirk: The division clincher Thursday in Cincinnati was an 8-2 win, then came four home runs in the eighth inning Friday on the 20th anniversary of the 4+1 Game for another 8-2 triumph. That was the first time in Dodgers history they’ve won consecutive games by an 8-2 score.

Monday: One day after a rare bad outing, Edgardo Henriquez was placed on the injured list with low back discomfort, ending his regular season and putting his playoff availability in question. Bobby Miller returned from Triple-A.
Wednesday: Trade deadline acquisition Kris Bubic was activated off the 60-day IL to make his Dodgers debut in relief, the team’s 33rd pitcher of the season. Gervase was optioned and Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Thursday: Miller was sent back to Oklahoma City, and Landon Knack was called up to pitch four scoreless innings in relief in the division clincher in Cincinnati.
Sunday: Sheehan got the call back up to the Dodgers, with Tarik Skubal placed on the bereavement list. Kyle Hurt was also called up, with Seth Halvorsen optioned.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Dave Roberts has a dilemma.
His first baseman, Freddie Freeman, just turned 37 years old and has been slumping badly down the stretch while playing through patellar tendinitis in his right knee. Never one to accept days off as the answer to anything, Freeman would probably benefit from some downtime this week – but he also needs at-bats to rediscover the swing that had him batting .300 for the season just two weeks ago or recalibrate it to accommodate his balky knee.
“There’s rest, but there’s also trying to find your swing,” Roberts acknowledged after putting Freeman in the lineup on Saturday and Sunday – a day game following a night game.
“I think it’s a work in progress,” Roberts said of Freeman’s swing. “The other day in Cincinnati (a three-hit game on Tuesday), I think it was looking pretty good, and then. I actually thought yesterday there were a couple good swings there.
“Obviously, the results weren’t there for him, and he’s frustrated, and I think that you just kind of have to count on him to figure it out and bet on him. And that’s kind of where we’re at. But again, having the week off (with a first-round bye) would be huge too.”
Freeman said he has been doing some different drills in the batting cage, focused on hitting the ball “out front” more.
“I feel like my faults are I try to hit the ball to the opposite field too much, and I let the ball get too deep, and it caused me to slide,” Freeman said earlier this week. “So today (in the cage) was – foot down early, catch the ball out front a little bit.”
Even with that three-hit game in Cincinnati and a two-hit game on Thursday, Freeman went into Sunday just 6 for his past 48 (.125), hitless in nine at-bats in the first two games of the series with the Giants.
“Got to go for results-based things right now,” Freeman said. “Looking to be hot for a few weeks. That’s all I’m trying to do.
“I’m just trying to find something that gives me results. We’re at the time where we’re just trying to get hot for five weeks here. So kind of like I did in the World Series a couple years ago (when his ankle was injured), I did the step-out move. That’s not sustainable over six months. I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable. I’m trying to find something that works for four weeks.”
OHTANI WORK
The “hope” is that Shohei Ohtani will be ready to come off the injured list when he is eligible on Wednesday, Roberts said. When he does, Roberts expects him to be in the lineup for the final five games.
“Absolutely,” Roberts said. “Yeah, he’ll need those live at-bats.”
Roberts has said Ohtani is “pain-free” but he acknowledged that Ohtani won’t be feeling 100% when he returns – but will be closer to it than he has been in weeks.
“Discomfort you can play through,” Roberts said of how Ohtani is feeling. “I think there’s a difference between discomfort and pain. Is it 100%? Probably not. Is it better than it was a week ago? Yes.
“Honestly I think that’s just a better question for Shohei to give more specifics, but I do think that when he’s activated it’s going to be the best physical place he’s been in in quite some time.”
Ohtani has spoken with the media just once in the past five weeks (before he went on the IL).
KIM CALL
Signed to a three-year, $12.5 million contract, South Korean infielder Hyeseong Kim has spent most of the second season of that contract in Triple-A where he hit .265 with a .682 OPS in 84 games. He hasn’t been up with the Dodgers since May but Roberts said Kim will be part of the “conversation” for the postseason roster.
“My expectation is Hyeseong will be here during the off week (next week) and potentially be a conversation for the postseason (roster) because he has the ability to run, to play defense, and steal a base,” Roberts said. “He’s in the conversation, yes.”
Kim was on the postseason roster last fall, appearing in just two games. It will be difficult to give him a spot on a bench that seems set with Alex Call, Hunter Feduccia, Miguel Rojas, Kiké Hernandez and Josue De Paula.
ROSTER MOVES
The Dodgers placed pitcher Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list on Sunday and recalled Emmet Sheehan from Triple-A to pitch ‘bulk’ in Sunday’s game.
Also, reliever Seth Halvorsen was returned to Triple-A and reliever Kyle Hurt was recalled.
Sheehan is still under consideration for a bullpen role on the postseason roster.

LOS ANGELES -- Before Sunday’s game, the Los Angeles Dodgers made several roster moves, recalling right-handed pitchers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt while optioning right-hander Seth Halvorsen. The club also placed left-hander Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list.
The Dodgers would go on to win 3-1, with Kris Bubic recording the victory for his fourth win of the season.
Giants rookie starter Matt Wilkinson kept the Dodgers in check for most of his outing, pitching five shutout innings while striking out six. He consistently kept the Dodgers’ lineup off balance and prevented them from generating much offensively.
For the Dodgers, however, the pitching staff put together a complete performance outside of the one run allowed by Jack Dreyer. Sheehan followed Dreyer and delivered an especially effective outing in his return to the roster.
The right-hander pitched 5.1 innings, allowing just one hit while striking out eight. Considering the struggles Sheehan has endured throughout the 2026 season, seeing him throw the ball this effectively was particularly encouraging after the many setbacks he has faced.
The outing also builds on what Sheehan did in his previous appearance on Sept. 13 against the Miami Marlins. He pitched six scoreless innings while striking out five before being optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City the following day. The Dodgers recalled him Sunday, and he immediately followed that previous performance with another strong showing.
It wasn’t until the sixth inning that the Dodgers finally got on the board. Tommy Edman hit a solo home run to right field, and Kiké Hernández followed with an RBI double in the seventh to give the Dodgers a 2-1 lead. The Dodgers would add additional insurance in the eighth when Max Muncy delivered an RBI single to give the Dodgers their final run of the game and a 3-1 lead.
Bubic also made an appearance, marking his second game with the Dodgers and his first at Dodger Stadium. He took over for Sheehan after the first out of the sixth inning and recorded the final two outs, striking out one of the two batters he faced.
Bubic, an All-Star in 2025, joined the Dodgers after being acquired at the trade deadline in August. Previously with the Kansas City Royals, Bubic carved out a role as one of the better left-handed starters in the American League while also proving capable of working out of the bullpen throughout his career.
That versatility is exactly what the Dodgers hope he can provide. The expectation is that Bubic could serve as a high-leverage reliever out of the bullpen once October arrives. His role could look similar to the one Justin Wrobleski had during the Dodgers’ 2025 playoff push, when Wrobleski was used as a reliever capable of covering multiple innings while remaining an effective arm.
Those plans have yet to be finalized, but Bubic’s previous experience gives the Dodgers another option to consider. The hope is that he can provide some stability to the bullpen during the final weeks of the regular season before the Dodgers determine their postseason roster.

Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles llamaron de vuelta al lanzador Emmet Sheehan como parte de una serie de movimientos en el roster el domingo, y está previsto que el derecho se encargue de la mayor parte del juego en el cierre de la serie contra los Gigantes de San Francisco.
Las cuatro transacciones involucraron a lanzadores de los Dodgers. También llamaron de vuelta a Kyle Hurt, colocaron a Tarik Skubal en la lista de duelo y enviaron a Seth Halvorsen a Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Movimientos en el roster de los Dodgers
Jack Dreyer abrirá mientras los Dodgers buscan la barrida ante sus rivales del Área de la Bahía, antes de cederle el turno a Sheehan.
"Hoy estamos armando esto un poco con las opciones disponibles. Creo que se trata más de lo que, en nuestra opinión, le da a Emmet la mejor oportunidad", comentó el mánager Dave Roberts.
El jardinero derecho Kyle Tucker no estará en la alineación después de salir de la victoria del sábado por 10-4 debido a un lanzamiento foul que le pegó en la rodilla derecha.
Lesiones y esperanzas de regreso
Los Dodgers esperan ver pronto de regreso a Shohei Ohtani tras su primera estancia en la lista de lesionados desde que se unió al equipo en 2024. Podría ocurrir durante una serie de tres juegos contra los San Diego Padres que comienza la noche del martes. "Aún está en el aire, pero esa es nuestra esperanza", señaló Roberts.
Ohtani está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho. También ha estado lidiando con molestias en la rodilla izquierda desde hace meses.
Expectativas sobre el regreso de Ohtani
Roberts cree que Ohtani llegará sin dolor a la última semana de la temporada regular, mientras los Dodgers presionan para asegurar un descanso y evitar la ronda de comodines.
"Creo que hay una diferencia entre molestia y dolor. ¿Está al 100 por ciento? Probablemente no. ¿Está mejor que hace una semana? Sí", manifestó Roberts.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers made a number of pitching moves ahead of Sunday’s series finale against the San Francisco Giants. Tarik Skubal, who started on Saturday, was placed on bereavement leave, which facilitated the return of Emmet Sheehan from Triple-A Oklahoma City. In addition, reliever Kyle Hurt was recalled and Seth Halvorsen optioned in a swap of right-handers in the bullpen.
Sheehan was just optioned on Monday and normally would have needed to stay in the minors for 15 days, but because he’s replacing a player on the bereavement list (or injured list or paternity list) that allows the right-hander to return early.
After getting sent down to Triple-A on August 3, Sheehan turned his season around, including winning Pacific Coast League pitcher of the month, and he allowed one run in 11 2/3 innings last week for the Dodgers before getting optioned to Oklahoma City so the Dodgers could use a fresh arm. In his last five outings — three in Triple-A, two with Dodgers — Sheehan has allowed only two runs in 29 innings with 39 strikeouts (36.4-percent strikeout rate) against only eight walks.
All 26 outings by Sheehan this season have been starts, but on Sunday he’ll follow an opener in left-hander Jack Dreyer. Sunday provides at least a practice run of Sheehan’s most likely role in the postseason, pitching in bulk relief.
“Emmet’s a part of the conversation,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday, “but if there is a role in the postseason it would be out of the ’pen.”
Bereavement leave lasts for a minimum of three days and up to seven, so Skubal wouldn’t be activated until Wednesday at the earliest. But considering the left-hander just started on Saturday, don’t expect him to be activated until his start day, likely next weekend in San Francisco.
Halvorsen has allowed nine runs in 10 innings with the Dodgers, including three home runs, with six strikeouts and two walks. He pitched a scoreless inning on Saturday, which was his third appearance in four days.
Hurt pitched a scoreless inning for Oklahoma City on Friday, his only appearance in the last week. Since getting optioned on September 5, Hurt pitched in three games for Oklahoma City, all scoreless innings. This season with the Dodgers, Hurt has a 4.33 ERA and 3.84 xERA in 43 games, with 56 strikeouts and 23 walks in 43 2/3 innings.
Saturday was his 15th day on optional assignment in Triple-A, making Sunday his first day eligible to return from the minors.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers recalled pitcher Emmet Sheehan as part of a series of roster moves Sunday, with the right-hander set to handle the bulk of their series finale against the San Francisco Giants.
All four transactions involved Dodgers pitchers. They also recalled Kyle Hurt, placed Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list and optioned Seth Halvorsen to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Jack Dreyer will start as the Dodgers go for the sweep against their Bay Area rivals before giving way to Sheehan, who is 5-8 with a 4.79 ERA in 22 games this season.
“Kind of piecing through the available options today,” manager Dave Roberts said. “I think it's just more of what gives Emmet, in our opinion, the best chance.”
Right fielder Kyle Tucker won't be in the lineup after coming out of Saturday's 10-4 victory because of a fouled pitch that went off his right knee. The early exit was described as precautionary, and Roberts felt it was worth giving him a day off, particularly with Tucker finding his stride after an erratic first season in Los Angeles. He is batting .429 with five homers, eight extra-base hits and 11 RBIs in his past 10 games.
The Dodgers expect to see Shohei Ohtani back soon after his first stint on the injured list since joining the team in 2024. It could come during a three-game series against the San Diego Padres that starts Tuesday night. “Still up in the air, but that’s our hope,” Roberts said.
Ohtani is on the 15-day IL with right biceps inflammation. He also has been dealing with left knee soreness for months.
Roberts believes Ohtani will be pain-free going into the last week of the regular season, with the Dodgers pushing to secure a bye to avoid the wild-card round.

Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles anunciaron varios movimientos en su cuerpo de lanzadores. El equipo colocó al zurdo Tarik Skubal en la lista de duelo, llamó a los derechos Emmet Sheehan y Kyle Hurt, y envió a Seth Halvorsen a las Ligas Menores.
El comunicado no ofreció detalles sobre la situación familiar de Skubal ni una fecha específica para su regreso.
El zurdo de 29 años viene de permitir cuatro carreras en cinco entradas durante su presentación de anoche. Desde que fue adquirido procedente de los Tigres de Detroit, ha realizado nueve aperturas con los Dodgers, con récord de 4-2 y efectividad de 2.95 en 55 innings.
En toda la temporada, Skubal acumula balance de 11-7 y promedio de carreras limpias de 2.85 en 25 aperturas. El ganador de dos premios Cy Young ha sido una pieza importante del pitcheo de Los Ángeles desde su llegada.
Emmet Sheehan regresa después de una salida dominante
Sheehan, de 26 años, lanzó seis entradas sin permitir carreras frente a los Marlins el pasado domingo. El derecho suma 22 aperturas esta temporada, la mayor cantidad de su carrera, y presenta récord de 5-8.
En 107 entradas ha ponchado a 123 bateadores y mantiene un WHIP de 1.21. Está en su tercera campaña con los Dodgers, organización que lo seleccionó en la sexta ronda del Draft de 2021, procedente de Boston College.
Su regreso le ofrece al equipo un brazo que viene de responder con una actuación dominante ante Miami.
Kyle Hurt recibe otra oportunidad con el equipo grande
Kyle Hurt también fue llamado y comienza su quinta estancia de la temporada con los Dodgers. El derecho de 28 años tiene marca de 4-1, efectividad de 4.33 y 56 ponches en 43 entradas y dos tercios durante esta campaña.
En sus tres temporadas con Los Ángeles acumula promedio de carreras limpias de 3.78, con 62 ponches en 52 entradas y un tercio.
Hurt fue seleccionado originalmente por los Marlins en la quinta ronda del Draft de 2020, procedente de la Universidad del Sur de California.
Seth Halvorsen baja a las menores
Por su parte, Halvorsen fue enviado a las Ligas Menores después de lanzar una entrada sin carreras y ponchar a dos bateadores anoche.
Aunque respondió en su presentación más reciente, el derecho de 26 años registra efectividad de 8.10 en 11 apariciones con los Dodgers, con una victoria y una derrota.
Antes de incorporarse a Los Ángeles, había participado en 21 encuentros con los Rockies de Colorado durante esta temporada, con marca de 0-1 y efectividad de 4.74.

One of the game's hardest throwers delivers ... a 32.6 mph HBP?
This browser does not support the video element.
No batter wants to be hit by a pitch, but if they are going to get plunked, they probably all want the pitch to be like the one that made contact with the Giants’ Drew Gilbert on Saturday against the Dodgers.
In the ninth inning of Los Angeles’ 10-4 victory, Dodgers reliever Seth Halvorsen threw a 1-2 pitch to Gilbert that hit the outfielder on his right thigh. But it probably didn’t leave a mark since the pitch registered at just 32.6 mph and bounced on its way toward the plate.
That makes it the slowest recorded pitch on a HBP in the pitch-tracking era (since 2008). It surpassed the previous record-holder, a 34.2 mph pitch from the Reds’ Jose Trevino that hit the Pirates’ Jake Mangum on May 2.
Halvorsen, who was optioned to Triple-A on Sunday among a series of Dodgers roster moves, is one of the game’s hardest throwers, with an average fastball velo of 98.9 mph. But he appeared to either slip or have one of his cleat spikes get caught in the mound. That took the right-hander completely out of his delivery, but he still lobbed the pitch toward home.
It’s been a big week for funny hit-by-pitches. Saturday’s blooper occurred one week after the Guardians’ Joey Cantillo hit the Twins’ Brooks Lee with a 39.9 mph offering.

The Los Angeles Dodgers recalled Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt, optioned Seth Halvorsen and placed Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list ahead of their series finale against the San Francisco Giants.
Skubal and Halvorsen both pitched on Saturday in the victory.
Skubal allowed four runs in five innings, showing a lot of frustration with his outing. He gave up eight hits and walked two while only striking out three.
He has made nine starts for the Dodgers since being acquired from the Detroit Tigers and he is 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA in 55 innings. On the season, he is 11-7 with a 2.85 ERA in 25 starts.
The two-time Cy Young award winner has been in the Major Leagues seven seasons, posting a 65-44 record with a 3.04 ERA in 162 games (159 starts). He has 1,065 strikeouts in 918.1 innings while owning a 1.02 WHIP.
Skubal must be on the bereavement list for a minimum of three days and a maximum of seven days. It’s unclear why he was placed on bereavement leave, but the list is used if the player has a death or serious illness in their family.
Halvorsen tossed a scoreless inning with two strikeouts to close out Saturday’s game.
He made 11 appearances with the Dodgers, going 1-1 with an 8.10 ERA. Before joining the Dodgers, he appeared in 21 games for the Colorado Rockies this year, posting an 0-1 record with a 4.74 ERA.
He has made 86 Major League appearances for the Rockies (2024-26) and Dodgers (2026), and he is 4-5 with a 4.78 ERA and 72 strikeouts in 81 innings.
Dodgers add reinforcements for bullpen game
Sheehan returns after pitching six scoreless innings against the Miami Marlins last Sunday. He has gone 5-8 with the Dodgers in 2026, posting a career-high 22 starts, racking up 123 strikeouts in 107 innings and a 1.21 WHIP.
He is in his third season with the Dodgers, recording a 4.23 ERA with a 15-12 record in 50 games (45 starts).
The Dodgers needed a pitcher who could throw the bulk of the game on Sunday, and Sheehan is likely to fulfill that role.
Hurt returns for his fifth stint with the team and provides them with another fresh arm before the bullpen game. He has gone 4-1 with a 4.33 ERA this season and 56 strikeouts in 43.2 innings.
He has been with the Dodgers three seasons, compiling a 3.78 ERA with 62 strikeouts in 52.1 innings and a 4-2 mark.

LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers made a flurry of roster moves before Sunday afternoon's series finale against the Giants, placing left-hander Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list, recalling right-handers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A Oklahoma City and optioning right-hander Seth Halvorsen.
The Dodgers also gave right fielder Kyle Tucker Sunday off after he fouled a ball off the lower knee/upper shin area on his right leg on Saturday night. Manager Dave Roberts does not think the soreness will become an ongoing issue for Tucker, who is expected back in the lineup on Tuesday.
Here's how these moves will impact the Dodgers on Sunday and beyond:
Skubal will be away from the team for "a couple days," Roberts said. Players may spend between three to seven days on the bereavement list, so Skubal might not miss his next start, which is projected to come on Friday in San Francisco.
"Some personal stuff going on," Roberts said, "but he's fine."
Skubal is 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA in nine starts since being dealt to L.A. ahead of the Trade Deadline.
Sheehan was set to pitch bulk innings on Sunday behind opener Jack Dreyer. The thought was that pitching Sheehan behind an opener could not only help him get deeper into the game, but also prepare him for a possible bullpen role in the postseason, which would be his only path to making the roster.
In his previous two starts for the Dodgers, Sheehan allowed one earned run across 11 2/3 innings. After a strong stint in Triple-A, he has looked to trend in the right direction in what has been an inconsistent season overall (5-8, 4.79 ERA).
Tucker has heated up at the end of the first season of his four-year, $240 million contract, which has been disappointing (his .728 OPS is on track to be a career-worst mark in a full season). Since Sept. 9, he's hitting 15-for-35 (.429) with five home runs and 35 total bases, his most in a 10-game span this season.
On Saturday, Tucker exited the game after six innings due to a combination of the hit-by-pitch and the lopsided score. He said he feels fine, but Roberts decided to give him an extra day to rest after Tucker had played the previous nine games without a day off.
"I feel like everyone's grinding at this point in the season," Tucker said. "But I'll be good with it."

BREAKING: Tarik Skubal will be away from the Dodgers for a couple days due to personal reasons ?
Seth Halvorsen has also been optioned and Kyle Hurt and Emmet Sheehan are back.
Skubal last pitched for the Dodgers on Saturday, and had a frustrating outing—his worst since donning a Dodgers uniform. He lasted just five innings, allowing four earned runs on eight hits while recording a season-low three strikeouts.
What Does Tarik Skubal's Absence Mean?
The left-hander's presence on the bereavement list doesn't impact the rest of the Dodgers' season, as he will likely be ready for his next turn through the rotation if he stays out for a couple of days as Roberts said.
That should be a huge relief for the Dodgers, who have quite a few injuries among their starters as the postseason nears. Shohei Ohtani, Roki Sasaki and Eric Lauer are all on the IL, leaving LA with limited options.
An injury or extended period of absence for any of their remaining starters would throw a wrench in their plans for the postseason.
Additionally, Skubal's track record since joining the team is fantastic—serving as one of their best starters since the beginning of August. He has a 2.95 ERA through nine starts, striking out 60 batters through 55 innings pitched.
What Roles Will Kyle Hurt and Emmet Sheehan Play?
Hurt and Sheehan are likely to jump straight into the action, as the Dodgers are running a bullpen game on Sunday.
Jack Dreyer is getting the start, but using Hurt and Sheehan—both of whom have experience handling bulk innings—afterwards is the Dodgers' most likely move.
The duo have bounced between Triple-A and MLB over the past few weeks, but could very well find a spot on the team if they perform well Sunday. Sheehan is in the midst of a fantastic run of form, and has capitalized on both of his MLB opportunities in Setpember.
He only allowed one earned run through 11.2 innings pitched over his last two starts, and is a real candidate to make the postseason roster despite his recent stays in the minors.
Before that, though, he'll have to perform in Sunday's game against the Giants, which begins at 1:10 p.m. PT.

The Los Angeles Dodgers announced a major roster move ahead of Sunday's series finale against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers have recalled right-handed pitchers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A. Sheehan will take down bulk innings on Sunday as LA looks to preserve the bullpen heading into the final week of the regular season.
As for the corresponding moves, left-handed pitcher Tarik Skubal was placed on the bereavement list and will be away from the team for "a couple days," per manager Dave Roberts. Additionally, right-hander Seth Halvorsen was optioned.
Dodgers Recall Emmet Sheehan, Kyle Hurt
Sheehan was surprisingly demoted this past week amid a dominant stretch of play.
Across his last two starts at the MLB level, Sheehan allowed just one run over 11.2 innings with 15 strikeouts.
“Man, Emmet’s been great. The last two have been fantastic,” Roberts said after he was sent down. “Emmet’s done everything he can do in his power to force our hand, which I love. ... The last two have been really good.”
Now, Sheehan is getting another opportunity to take down bulk innings and audition for a spot on the postseason roster. If he has another strong outing, he'll likely secure a spot in the postseason bullpen as a multi-inning option.
As for Hurt, he's been up and down multiple times this season. The right-hander has made 43 appearances at the big league level, compiling a 4.33 ERA with 56 strikeouts to 23 walks over 43.2 innings of work.
He's unlikely to factor into the team's October plans, but could take down innings over the final week of the regular season.
Dodgers Place Tarik Skubal on Bereavement List, Option Seth Halvorsen
Skubal will deal with a personal matter for the next couple days, but should be back in time to make one more start before the conclusion of the regular season.
He pitched on Saturday, allowing four runs over five innings with three strikeouts.
As for Halvorsen, he's made 11 appearances at the big league level for the Dodgers this season, accruing an 8.10 ERA with six strikeouts to two walks over 10 innings of work.
He was acquired by the Dodgers a couple weeks before the trade deadline in a three-player deal with the Colorado Rockies. He likely won't return to the big league club for the remainder of the year.

CINCINNATI -- Try as they might to view 2026 as its own season, everything the Dodgers have done this year is impossible to separate from the larger context of what they have accomplished in more than a decade of excellence.
The Dodgers hit another key milestone in their title defense by reclaiming the NL West crown with an 8-2 victory over the Reds on Thursday afternoon at Great American Ball Park. Three days after their traditional champagne toast in honor of clinching a postseason berth, winning the West brought on a wild clubhouse celebration -- which they hope will be the first of many over the next several weeks.
"You get so mired in each year, it’s hard to have any perspective," president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said. "We’ve had our share of troubles this year. Things where we had to work harder than we expected on a couple of fronts. But the important thing is how we finish and how we go into October."
In their record-tying 14 consecutive postseason appearances, the Dodgers have 13 division titles. The only team to unseat them was the 2021 Giants, who edged them in one of the most highly contested NL West races in recent memory.
Since divisional play began in 1969, the Dodgers lead all big league teams with 24 division titles, one more than the Braves -- currently in line to win the NL East -- and three more than the Yankees. Each year's achievements raise the bar for every ensuing year. The expectations facing the Dodgers have become nearly impossible to meet. But they've embraced them gladly.
"There is certainly a higher expectation when, if you don't win the World Series, you fail," manager Dave Roberts said. "But that's kind of part of what you signed up with the Dodgers.”
The Dodgers' offense, whose inconsistency has been a perpetual concern over the course of the season, provided plenty of early support to back a scheduled bullpen game. Kyle Tucker led the way with a four-hit, three-RBI showing, finishing a triple shy of the Dodgers’ first cycle since 2017. Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, Josue De Paula and Miguel Rojas also knocked in runs.
Justin Wrobleski opened the bullpen game with three perfect innings, and while Blake Treinen surrendered a solo home run in the fourth, Landon Knack pitched four scoreless frames before Seth Halvorsen allowed a run in the ninth.
With nine games remaining in the regular season, the Dodgers are far from full strength. Their best hitter, Shohei Ohtani, is on the 15-day IL, as is first-time All-Star Andy Pages. The six-man rotation they carried for most of the season has been reduced to four fully stretched-out starters on the active roster, necessitating Thursday's bullpen game.
"It's been the same thing the last couple years," Muncy said. "We've had guys go down. We've had guys step up in their place. … That's all that we ask, and we've been able to survive a lot."
The Dodgers are expecting reinforcements back before the postseason, and would greatly benefit from securing a first-round bye to advance directly to the NL Division Series -- giving them five days off after the end of the regular season. They hold a four-game lead over the Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League.
This edition of the Dodgers is not without its flaws, but then again, neither were the back-to-back champion teams in 2024 and '25. After becoming the first team in a quarter-century to defend their title last year, they will vie for the Majors' first three-peat since the 1998-2000 Yankees.
While the talk of a three-peat began almost from the moment the Dodgers became back-to-back champions last November, Roberts urged his team to stay focused on the present while keeping the larger goal in mind. In his annual speech on the first day of full-squad workouts during Spring Training, he delivered the following message: Be a greyhound, looking forward with blinders on.
Tarik Skubal was not a Dodger when Roberts gave his spring address, but he saw the message play out after he was dealt to L.A. ahead of the Trade Deadline. He arrived at the beginning of a season-high seven-game losing streak -- and the tough stretch gave him a feel for the culture that has led to his new team's sustained success.
"I think there was no panic from this group," Skubal said. "I think that’s why in big moments, pressure doesn't really get to these guys."
The Dodgers have a long road ahead as they look to get back to the World Series, but it bears similarities to the roads they have traveled before. The slate might be wiped clean every year, but they have experience weathering the challenges along the way to the promised land.
"It's a different year, but I think it's kind of the same," Mookie Betts said. "The same group of guys. We know what to expect. We know what to expect from each other. It's the same goal every year. Getting here, you can't really get too focused on how, as long as you get there."

The Los Angeles Dodgers were already playoff-bound for the 14th straight season. But after taking down the Cincinnati Reds 8-2 on Thursday, they're winners of the NL West for the 13th time in that span and for the fifth season in a row.
Of course, the streak LA cares about most will be at stake in the postseason. The Dodgers are aiming to become the first team to three-peat as World Series champions since the fabled New York Yankees of 1998-2000.
With the victory Thursday, the Dodgers (93-60) have the second-best record in the NL, behind only the Milwaukee Brewers (95-58), who clinched the NL Central earlier this week but dropped their series finale to the Pirates on Thursday. The Dodgers and Brewers will jockey for the NL's top seed over the final week of the regular season.
Meanwhile, LA will do its best to sort out an injury-riddled roster before the calendar flips to October. Most notably, the status of Shohei Ohtani will be acutely monitored, as the two-way star has been juggling issues with his biceps, left knee and neck.
Then there's lefty starting pitcher Blake Snell, who's dealing with a groin injury that ended his start Wednesday versus the Reds after just one inning.
Andy Pages is expected back in the Dodgers' outfield soon. However, only time will tell how quickly he returns to form after healing from a fractured left hand.
A bullpen game and a flurry of early scoring sealed the NL West in Cincy
LA didn't need one of its aces to secure the division title on Thursday. Manager Dave Roberts, who has overseen 10 of the Dodgers' NL West crowns amid this memorable run, opted for a bullpen game.
Lefty Justin Wrobleski spun three innings of shutout ball. He was the first to punch out Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz, who clocked out with three Ks on the day. Cincinnati's lone run came in the fourth, when Sal Stewart homered off Dodgers right-handed hurler Blake Treinen.
Then righty Landon Knack registered four scoreless innings while allowing four hits. Seth Halvorsen finished the game while allowing one more Reds run to score in the ninth.
That merely made a dent in LA's commanding lead. The Dodgers built that in large part thanks to a trio of extra-base hits. Kyle Tucker went yard in the first inning, depositing a two-run dinger. He also hit an RBI double in the second. In the fourth, Max Muncy drove home a pair of runs with a two-bagger.
The Reds and Dodgers traded runs in the ninth, with Miguel Rojas taking one deep to put the exclamation point on LA's division-clinching victory.

Catorce clasificaciones consecutivas a la postemporada. Cinco títulos divisionales seguidos. La inusual oportunidad de luchar por un tricampeonato de la Serie Mundial.
Los Dodgers alcanzaron otro hito importante en la defensa de su título al recuperar la corona del Oeste de la Liga Nacional con una victoria de 8-2 sobre los Rojos la tarde del jueves en el Great American Ball Park. Tres días después de su tradicional brindis con champaña para celebrar que aseguraron un lugar en la postemporada, conquistar el Oeste desató una eufórica celebración en el clubhouse, que esperan sea la primera de muchas durante las próximas semanas.
En sus 14 participaciones consecutivas en la postemporada, igualando un récord, los Dodgers han conquistado 13 títulos divisionales. El único equipo que logró destronarlos fueron los Gigantes del 2021, que los superaron por estrecho margen en una de las luchas por el Oeste de la Liga Nacional más reñidas de los últimos tiempos.
La ofensiva de los Dodgers, cuya inconsistencia ha sido una preocupación constante a lo largo de la temporada, brindó bastante respaldo desde temprano para apoyar un juego de bullpen programado. Kyle Tucker encabezó el ataque con cuatro hits y tres carreras impulsadas, quedándose a un triple de conseguir el primer ciclo de los Dodgers desde el 2017. Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, el dominicano Josué De Paula y el venezolano Miguel Rojas también remolcaron anotaciones.
Justin Wrobleski abrió el juego de bullpen con tres innings perfectos, y aunque Blake Treinen permitió un jonrón solitario en el cuarto episodio, Landon Knack lanzó cuatro entradas en blanco antes de que Seth Halvorsen concediera una rayita en el noveno acto.
Con nueve juegos restantes en la temporada regular, los Dodgers están lejos de contar con todo su plantel. Su mejor bateador, Shohei Ohtani, está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días, al igual que el cubano Andy Pagés, llamado por primera vez al Juego de Estrellas. La rotación de seis abridores que utilizaron durante gran parte de la temporada se ha reducido a cuatro abridores completamente acondicionados en el róster activo, lo que hizo necesario recurrir a un juego de bullpen el jueves.
Los Dodgers esperan recuperar refuerzos antes de la postemporada y se beneficiarían enormemente de asegurar el descanso en la primera ronda para avanzar directamente a la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional, lo que les daría cinco días libres después del final de la temporada regular. Tienen una ventaja de 4.0 juegos sobre los Bravos por el segundo puesto de la Liga Nacional.
Esta versión de los Dodgers no está exenta de defectos, pero tampoco lo estuvieron los equipos campeones consecutivos del 2024 y 2025. Después de convertirse el año pasado en el primer equipo en un cuarto de siglo en defender con éxito su título, buscarán el primer tricampeonato de Grandes Ligas desde los Yanquis de 1998 al 2000.
“Tenemos tanta hambre como en el 2024 y 2025”, dijo el piloto Dave Roberts. “Esta es una temporada aparte. Nuestros muchachos lo entienden”.

Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Cincinnati Reds 8-2 on Thursday, September 17th, to clinch the National League West.
Kyle Tucker’s big day
Tucker has been fantastic lately, and Thursday’s game was a true cherry on top. He went 4-for-5 with two doubles, a home run, and a single, and drove in three runs.
Over the last seven games, Tucker has put up a .375/.467/.917 slash line with three home runs, nine RBIs, five walks, and three strikeouts.
Even over the last 15 games, Tucker is hitting .280/.383/.680 with five home runs and 11 RBIs.
Tucker nearly had a cycle, but when he gapped a ball in the eighth inning, he didn’t push for a triple and held up instead.
Still, this was Tucker’s game and a promising sign of things to come.
It was not just Tucker who played well, though; Freddie Freeman went 2-for-3 with an RBI and a walk, while Max Muncy went 2-for-4 with two RBIs.
Additionally, Miguel Rojas added the eighth run with a solo home run in the top of the ninth.
Considering the Dodgers went 0-for-11 with runners in scoring position on Wednesday, Thursday’s game was a welcome development.
Bullpen bounce-back
Justin Wrobleski looked great for three innings, allowing no hits and pitching them all perfect, with three strikeouts.
He was only at 32 pitches, and if Roberts wanted to stretch him out, he could have, but the Dodgers want to save his best stuff for the postseason.
Additionally, Landon Knack handled the bulk of the relief, allowing just four hits and recording two punchouts over four innings of clean work.
Blake Treinen and Seth Halvorsen each allowed a run, but thanks to Knack and Wrobleski, it was more than enough to finally clinch the division.

CINCINNATI (AP) — Elly De La Cruz hit a two-run homer and the Cincinnati Reds at least temporarily prevented the Los Angeles Dodgers from clinching the NL West title with a 6-2 victory on Wednesday night.
The Dodgers (92-60) needed a win or a loss by San Diego to win their fifth straight NL West crown and 13th in 14 seasons. The Padres played at Colorado later Wednesday.
Left-hander Blake Snell started for the Dodgers but departed after one inning with left groin tightness. Snell, who threw a no-hitter for the Giants in his last appearance in Great American Ball Park, faced three batters, allowing a hit with a strikeout on 19 pitches.
Blake Treinen took over in the second as the first of six relievers used by Los Angeles.
Mookie Betts singled off Andrew Abbott in the third and scored on Will Smith's double to put the Dodgers ahead 1-0. Abbott allowed a run on three hits with five walks in 4 2/3 innings. Tejay Antone (3-2), the third of six Cincinnati pitchers, got the last out of the sixth.
De La Cruz's homer off Seth Halvorsen (1-2), his 28th of the season, put the Reds ahead 2-1 in the third. It was De La Cruz's fifth longball against the Dodgers this season, most of any opposing player.
Dane Myers' homer off Bobby Miller, his seventh, extended the Reds' lead to 3-1 in the fifth.
Juan Brito's RBI single made it 4-2 in the sixth.
TJ Friedl singled with the bases loaded in the seventh to drive in two runs. Sal Stewart was thrown out at the plate by Dodgers center fielder Tommy Edman to end the inning.
The Dodgers stranded 12 runners and went 0 for 11 with runners in scoring position.
Up next
RHP Brady Singer (6-14, 5.38 ERA) will start Thursday's series finale for the Reds. The Dodgers had not announced their starter.

CINCINNATI -- El zurdo Blake Snell abandonó su apertura contra los Rojos debido a rigidez en la ingle izquierda, luego de lanzar apenas un inning en la derrota por 6-2 la noche del miércoles en el Great American Ball Park.
Snell tiene antecedentes de problemas similares. En 2024, cuando estaba con los Gigantes, ingresó dos veces a la lista de lesionados debido a una distensión en la ingle izquierda y otra en el aductor izquierdo. Antes de eso, también perdió tiempo de juego por lesiones en el aductor en 2021 y 2022.
El derecho Blake Treinen comenzó a calentar en la parte alta del segundo inning y relevó a Snell en la parte baja del episodio. Eso obligó a los Dodgers a recurrir de manera inesperada a un juego de bullpen, utilizando a seis relevistas un día antes de que tuvieran previsto emplear esa misma estrategia en el último encuentro de la serie en Cincinnati el jueves.
Los Dodgers llegaron al miércoles necesitando una victoria sobre los Rojos o una derrota de los Padres en Colorado para conquistar su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en los últimos 14 años. Tras la derrota, tendrán dos cosas que seguir de cerca durante el resto de la noche: el resultado de San Diego y el estado de Snell.
Snell realizó 19 pitcheos y enfrentó al mínimo de bateadores en el primer inning. Permitió un sencillo de Sal Stewart con dos outs, pero el novato fue puesto fuera posteriormente en una jugada de viraje e intento de robo. Snell lanzó ocho rectas de cuatro costuras con una velocidad promedio de 94.5 mph, 1.5 mph por debajo de su promedio de la temporada.
Esta temporada, Snell ha estado dos veces en la lista de lesionados. Comenzó el año fuera de acción por fatiga en el hombro izquierdo y regresó a la lista de lesionados después de una apertura debido a cuerpos libres en el codo izquierdo, que fueron retirados quirúrgicamente.
Snell había estado dominante desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados el 11 de agosto, con marca de 4-0 y efectividad de 1.04 en seis aperturas antes del miércoles. No permitió más de una carrera en ninguna de esas salidas y los Dodgers ganaron todas menos una. Su ausencia se hizo sentir cuando el bullpen tuvo que encargarse de los últimos siete innings, con Seth Halvorsen, Bobby Miller y Jack Dreyer permitiendo dos carreras cada uno.

Snell has a history of similar issues, twice going on the injured list with a left groin strain and a left adductor strain in 2024 when he was with the Giants. Before that, he also missed time with adductor injuries in '21 and '22.
Right-hander Blake Treinen began warming up in the top of the second inning and relieved Snell in the bottom half of the frame. It became an unscheduled bullpen game, with the Dodgers using six relievers the day before they had been planning to run a bullpen game in Thursday's finale in Cincinnati.
The Dodgers entered Wednesday needing either a win over the Reds or a Padres loss in Colorado to clinch their 13th NL West title in the past 14 years. After their loss, they'll have two things to monitor for the remainder of the evening: San Diego's outcome and Snell's status.
Snell threw 19 pitches while facing the minimum in the first inning, giving up a two-out single to Sal Stewart before the rookie was erased on a pickoff-caught stealing. Snell threw eight four-seamers with an average velocity of 94.5 mph, down 1.5 mph from his season average.
This season, Snell has been on the injured list twice. He was sidelined by left shoulder fatigue to open the year and landed back on the IL after one start with loose bodies in his left elbow, which were surgically removed.
Snell had been dominant since returning from the IL on Aug. 11, going 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA in six starts entering Wednesday. He allowed no more than one run in each of those starts, and the Dodgers won all but one of them. His absence was felt when the bullpen had to cover the final seven innings, with Seth Halvorsen, Bobby Miller and Jack Dreyer allowing two runs apiece.
